extracted_fields.objective: To analyze decadal Land Use Land Cover (LULC) changes in Taiwan from 1990 to 2020 and simulate future LULC for 2030 and 2050 using machine learning (Support Vector Machine) and Markov chain models under multiple scenarios, incorporating demographic factors and environmental variables.
extracted_fields.land_use_classes: Barren; Uncultivated; Water Deep; Water Shallow; Built-up; Forest; Cultivated
extracted_fields.predictors: Aspect; Elevation; Hillshade; Distance to Rivers; Distance to Roads; Slope
extracted_fields.population_selected: Yes; Taiwan’s demographic shifts including negative population growth are considered in modeling future LULC and carbon emissions
extracted_fields.tools_software_used: Not explicitly specified; use of Google Earth Engine for image processing implied; GIS for spatial data processing; SVM and Markov Chain modeling software/tools implied
extracted_fields.validation_methods: Confusion matrix; Accuracy assessment metrics including producer’s accuracy, user’s accuracy, overall accuracy, Kappa coefficient; Root-mean-square-error (RMSE); Validation of predicted 2020 LULC against actual 2020 classified data
extracted_fields.validation_data_sources: Ground Control Points (GCPs) totaling 655 points for classification validation; 300 GCPs for predicted 2020 LULC validation
extracted_fields.scalability: Yes; national-scale approach and integrated SVM-Markov modeling framework applicable to other regions with similar urbanization and environmental complexity
